purpose: Bounded discovery of possible omissions, not canonical admission or a completed source audit.
reviewer: AI-assisted reviewer, AI-assisted research; no human classification approval recorded
scope: English substantive Parliament AI resolutions outside the AI Act procedure and selected EDPB, FRA, ENISA and Europol reports/opinions. EDPS retrieval attempts and earlier EU-OSHA/Frontex backlog are recorded as limitations. Contemporary collection only in this bounded result; the approved historical boundary remains unrestricted.
conventions: All candidates remain research suggestions. Discovery status is not an inventory decision or publication approval.
All main candidate records below had an official primary English HTML or PDF opened and relevant passages reviewed. This does not mean every page was read.
Document-date meaning is stated per record. Report publication dates are used as explicit fallbacks where the report supplies only its year; unknown precise issue dates are not invented.
For Parliament records publication_date is the OJ manifestation actually read, not an assertion of first online publication.
All sector and provenance values are provisional researcher classifications. Institutional adoption or official hosting alone does not prove named authorship.
No full-text files were downloaded or retained and no file hashes were verified. Retrieved text is tool evidence, not a local archive.

candidates.title: European Parliament resolution of 20 October 2020 with recommendations to the Commission on a framework of ethical aspects of artificial intelligence, robotics and related technologies
candidates.publication_date_meaning: OJ C 404, p. 63; date visible in the opened EUR-Lex text.
candidates.evidence_locator: Heading and OJ date at HTML lines 294–309; paragraphs 109–114, heading 'Employment, workers’ rights, digital skills and the workplace', lines 823–839.
candidates.relevance_note: Dedicated ethical framework recommendations; paragraphs 109–110 address AI worker monitoring and recruitment, written notice and human review of automated human-resource decisions.
candidates.institution_note: European Parliament adopted the resolution; EUR-Lex hosts the OJ manifestation. Authorship tag is provisional for the institutional adopted text.
remaining_checks: Approve exact principal-record/annex treatment for the detailed recommendations; do not describe the proposed regulation in the annex as enacted law.
Verify relationships to separately citable committee reports before any admission.

candidates.title: European Parliament resolution of 20 October 2020 with recommendations to the Commission on a civil liability regime for artificial intelligence

remaining_checks: Resolve annex treatment and evidenced relationship to the 2022 AI Liability Directive proposal already present.
